why: The per-tick worker boot contract has three readers and they must not drift:
cloud/sandbox/worker.sh (the container), internal/sandbox/worker.go (tk, and
what the repository's tests check), and cloud/factory/src/worker-boot.ts (the
control plane, which tells worker-dispatch.ts what to run and what its probe
must see). This file is what both suites pin themselves to, the same way
sandbox-image-cases.json pins the two readers of [sandbox].image — a fix that
lands in one language and not the other is the failure this repository has
already paid for once.
The boot and finish PHASE args and markers (boot_arg, finish_arg, boot_marker,
boot_prompt_begin, boot_prompt_end) are the pi-durable worker host's half of
the same contract (epic 43y, tick pom): the host runs `--boot` as the env's
first command, submits the prompt it prints between the prompt markers to a
pi-durable conversation, and runs `--finish` with the conversation's outcome
once it settles. The boot's exit codes are the all-in-one's own (2-8, 13-15),
and the finish's are 9/10/11 below — a host that invents its own spelling
drifts the way the probe marker once nearly did.
The SETUP entry (setup_arg, epic 43y, tick i3h) is the restore's half: the
host rebuilds a lost container's workspace from the last wip snapshot and
runs `--setup` as the workspace's setup command, so the repository's own
[sandbox] setup (its dependency installs) is re-run in the restored box —
the one boot step the restore's git plumbing cannot re-run for itself. Its
exit classes are the boot's own (2, 3, 6); it pushes and clones nothing.
The REVIEW boot and finish (review_boot_*, review_finish_*, tick 8gd) are
the same shape for the PR-review job, whose conversation is hosted on the
run's WorkerAgent like every other cloud worker's: the orchestrator image
answers `--boot` in the review phase by running the review's setup (clone,
the pull request fetched as a ref, the model probe) and printing the review
prompt between the review prompt markers, and `--finish` afterwards posts
the findings file to the factory's review door. The marker line carries the
same two fields the worker's carries — branch= the ref that was reviewed,
result= the findings path the finish posts — and the prompt markers are the
review's own, so a reader can tell a review handoff from a worker's. The
commands are the orchestrator image's, not the worker's: a review boots
from the same entrypoint the epic orchestrator does (image/entrypoint.sh),
which is why its exit classes are the all-in-one's own (2-8, 12), and its
finish's 12 (EXIT_REVIEW) is the findings that never reached the factory.
The trace id (tick hyi) is what joins 'a message arrived' to 'a container
did this'. It reaches a container as TICKS_TRACE_ID, and it heads that
container's own R2 log stream as a banner line.
The banner is written by the CONTROL PLANE at dispatch, before the container
is addressed — not printed by the container. That is the whole point: the
container is the thing being diagnosed, and a banner a crashed container
never got far enough to print is a banner missing from exactly the log
anyone is reading. The container prints its own line too, which is
corroboration rather than the record, and it is why the marker below is
shared by all three readers instead of spelled twice.
The trace id's FORMAT (prefix, width, pattern) is pinned in
tracker-layout.json, beside the tick record field it is written into.

boundary.tk_denied: tk is not available to a worker agent
